g.title: j3172702861
g.text: I suppose it is oddly romantic, if a titch... dystopic, to go to such lengths to win the heart (and/or body) of your intended.

g.title: j110710398
g.text: Or is it even worse than that, and you were simply curious to see what might happen? And you are simply sitting there, plucking the legs off insects? We have sorted out the "what" behind your actions. Now I am attempting to interrogate the "why."

g.text: Mm, yes. Well, you likely have not had to contend with another protoframe whose memories are... split apart, in such a fashion as mine. In such a way, I suppose I am mildly sympathetic.

g.title: j1694648096
g.text: Aaah, I see... used to doing this devoid of all consequences. Well, you likely have not had to contend with another protoframe whose memories are... split apart, in such a fashion as mine.

g.title: j1104425317
g.text: Mm, yes. Well, you likely have not had to contend with another protoframe whose memories are... split apart, in such a fashion as mine. In such a way, I suppose I am mildly sympathetic. And all in the name of "love."

g.title: j365355293
g.text: And thus, I am beginning to understand how you came to "screw up" in the first place, Usurper.

g.title: j3006720642

g.title: j1620831451
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j3772047713->j1620831451

g.title: j3275360740
g.text: I would chastise you for what you have done in the name of getting what you want, but I am struck that the Orokin have been known to do far worse if not more creative.

g.title: j3503268959
g.text: You did, of course. Or rather, the children. The Tenno. Sometimes, I wonder if it was inevitable, what happened. Or if he could have been convinced to change his course.

g.title: j3695285869
g.text: Perhaps you are right. Or perhaps we are all, in the end, raw jewels. We have our flaws, our characteristics. Veins here, blemishes there.

g.title: j3960361086
g.text: And thus, I am beginning to understand how you came to "screw up" in the first place, Usurper. I have a hard time thinking you've done this in the name of "love."

g.title: j740318071
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j910365939
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j1646847578->j910365939

g.title: j3826348410
g.text: But the Orokin have always had a strange way of expressing their emotions, I suppose.

g.title: j701743352
g.text: I would chastise you for what you have done in the name of so-called "love" but I am struck that the Orokin have been known to do far worse if not more creative.

g.title: j3940519999
g.text: I would council sitting quietly with ones mistakes and accepting defeat for what it is, but that would make me quite the raging hypocrite, wouldn't it?

g.title: j331877812
g.text: I would council sitting quietly with ones mistakes and accepting defeat for what it is, personally. But I do not have the Void-given gift of looping pockets if time and erasing minds.

g.title: j1943323784
g.text: Have I told you the story of Ballas and Margulis? I am relying on you to be honest with me, as I have absolutely no way of knowing the truth otherwise.

g.title: j3453681587
g.text: I like to believe that we are all in the end, raw jewels. We have our flaws, our characteristics. Veins here, blemishes there.

g.title: j1131135386
g.text: And we may be faceted certain ways to either catch the light and set into elaborate works of art... or sharpened into weapons... or shattered into dust.

g.title: j532840304
g.text: I would council sitting quietly with ones mistakes and accepting defeat for what it is, but that would make me quite the raging hypocrite, wouldn't it?

g.title: j3346789129
g.text: I would council sitting quietly with ones mistakes and accepting defeat for what it is, personally. But I do not have the Void-given gift of looping pockets if time and erasing minds.

g.title: j1504674811
g.text: And who is to say that I would not have made good use of the Void-given gift of looping pockets of time and erasing minds?

g.title: j1872374895
g.text: How... exactly does this work, anyway?

g.title: j78674407
g.text: And how I despise that, let me tell you.

g.title: j2398825478
g.text: Perhaps that is a naïve belief, and we are all indeed immutable. You would know better than I, or so I hear.

g.title: j1049774797
g.text: And who is to say that I would not have made good use of the Void-given gift of looping pockets of time and erasing minds?

g.title: j388916108
g.text: How... exactly does this work, anyway?

g.title: j337939950
g.text: You're Infested, now. And you share a connection to the Infested strains that were used to create all Protoframe serum batches.

g.title: j2259882795
g.text: A talking guitar owes me some favors.

g.title: j3552854306
g.text: I have heard it.

g.title: j3410032973
g.text: I have heard it, but please, go on.

g.title: j473374109
g.text: I haven't heard it, actually.

g.title: j3506765509
g.text: No, I haven't heard the story, which... is actually part of why we're here. I know I missed opportunities the first time around.

g.title: j2762738141
g.text: But you have me telling this all out of order. Allow me to start properly.

g.title: j1259539386
g.text: You're Infested, now. And you share a connection to the Infested strains that were used to create all Protoframe serum batches.

g.title: j695196258
g.text: A talking guitar owes me some favors.

g.title: j3614152061
g.text: As far as I've been told - and she's not exactly entirely reliable, so take this with a grain of salt - the strains of Infestation for each of the batches of Protoframes can be influenced individually.

g.title: j3765137031
g.text: I... see.

g.title: j2097555904
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j894526986
g.text: Either you are attempting to appeal to my ego, which I commend you for, or you are simply extremely uninspired with your day. Which, as someone who has also enjoyed countless cycles of life, I nearly sympathize with.

g.title: j4269613021
g.text: Fascinating. You are either lying, or I still have stones you have yet left unturned. Which may be the reason you are here once more rereading fields already ploughed.

g.title: j418211723
g.text: Mm, little by little, you are nearly convincing me to forgive you for this mess you've made.

g.title: j3948523575
g.text: Long before the Zariman Ten Zero launched, and the Tenno were even a blip on the proverbial screen, Margulis the Archimedean and Ballas met during the opening of a new domed conservatory.

g.title: j1112044021
g.text: As far as I've been told - and she's not exactly entirely reliable, so take this with a grain of salt - the strains of Infestation for each of the batches of Protoframes can be influenced individually.

g.title: j4216235593
g.text: I... see.

g.title: j3172414489
g.text: As each one sort of lives inside its own "continuity" or time. All the Infestation strains are connected, but they sort of live in... nodules. It's all very complicated.

g.title: j918750982
g.text: The universe has certainly become stranger since I left it...

g.title: j2146202908
g.text: Then I shall not tire you by recounting the saga yet again, and I shall leave you to find other amusements with the rest of your day.

g.title: j3583173394
g.text: Were I not the subject of your amusement.

g.title: j1248323048
g.text: But? Regardless...

g.title: j2864192484
g.text: Boolean RoatheResetForgiven is now true.

g.title: j3672372248
g.text: Ballas was there for the sake of ceremony - we do love our pomp and circumstance, of course - and Margulis was desperately attempting not to be noticed.

g.title: j3847091830
g.text: As each one sort of lives inside its own "continuity" or time. All the Infestation strains are connected, but they sort of live in... nodules. It's all very complicated.

g.title: j2674243828
g.text: The universe has certainly become stranger since I left it...

g.title: j2622403260
g.text: So because I can loop time, I can loop Infestation "Batches" in a limited way.

g.title: j1892873410
g.text: You have no idea.

g.title: j3809425637
g.text: She rather takes the cake. Well... never mind.

g.title: j2888030837
g.text: Boolean RoatheMargulis1 is now true.

g.title: j1029517302
g.text: Ballas and Margulis.

g.title: j259166619
g.text: Something you must understand, my Usurper, is that Ballas had no reason to associate with her. No reason at all, unless his infatuation were genuine.

g.title: j2618540238
g.text: So because I can loop time, I can loop Infestation "Batches" in a limited way.

g.title: j1368514362
g.text: You have no idea.

g.title: j3780239027
g.text: She rather takes the cake. Well... never mind.

g.title: j575751138
g.text: And "she" is?

g.title: j2556712122
g.text: It was not just lust, for he could have whomever he wished - and did, quite often. If he wanted her, he could have simply had her and been done with her.

g.title: j4136372837
g.text: And "she" is?

g.title: j2908046103
g.text: Regardless. All this, in the name of "love?"

g.title: j2687931486
g.text: Lizzie. She'd love you.

g.title: j1802426647
g.text: A talking guitar.

g.title: j1212611822
g.text: He was an Executor. One of the most powerful of the Seven, in fact. He could have summoned her to his bedchambers and she would have been there without a second thought.

g.title: j3907790852
g.text: Lizzie. She'd love you.

g.title: j1673530550
g.text: A talking guitar.

g.title: j2168657638
g.text: But that is not what he did. Ballas took one look at her that evening, and... he was stricken, Drifter. Positively and absolutely beside himself.

g.title: j3715227492
g.text: I had never seen anything like it. It was as though no one else in the room even existed, save for Margulis. He seemed even... somehow too shy to speak to her. Him! Ballas!

g.title: j1101555636
g.text: Really?

g.title: j1163412680
g.text: You're making this up.

g.title: j2205701870
g.text: I swear on whatever remains of my honor! And what reason would I have to lie? What do I care of your opinion of the validity of their relationship?

g.title: j3008857999
g.text: I swear on whatever remains of my honor I am not! And what reason would I have to lie? What do I care of your opinion of the validity of their relationship?

g.title: j31484749
g.text: It simply saddens me that you lot would so quickly simplify something that is decidedly far more complicated than you would have it.

g.title: j233690379
g.text: They were in love, whether you wish to believe it or not. Ballas eshewed all class rules and tradition to take as his lover - and his sole romantic companion - an Archimedean.

g.title: j360327141
g.text: Only true love could have sent a man so spectacularly mad as it sent him, when it all went so very wrong...

g.title: j3566410436
g.text: How do you figure? Wasn't he responsible for her death?

g.title: j3737723959
g.text: Ballas was the one who had her executed.

g.title: j813460971
g.text: First, let us assume all you know is correct, and that his actions there were purely of his own accord. Let us assume that there were no other political maneuverings or blackmail or anything else being done behind the scenes that may have forced his hand.

g.title: j3826738499
g.text: Even if that were to be the case, and Ballas called for her execution entirely without influence, consider that it was already too late. The betrayal he felt had already cleaved him in two.

g.title: j1936480468
g.text: His heart and his mind was already broken.

g.title: j1277345103
g.text: I am not going to start feeling bad for him, if that's what you're asking me to do.

g.title: j1015540976
g.text: Because of the Tenno? Or because of what they did to her?

g.title: j1871237074
g.text: I am not asking you to have anything of the sort! Ballas deserves anything but whatever piss you can spare to spend on wherever you buried his corpse - if he even has a grave.

g.title: j2716776054
g.text: In a way, both. And in a way, neither. He was driven to madness that day, when he called for her execution. In fact, I would not be surprised if some part of him did not entirely recall doing the deed.

g.title: j2261986942
g.text: I am merely stating that on the day he called for her execution, he was a madman. I would not be surprised if some part of him did not entirely recall doing the deed, after the fact.

g.title: j3707815316
g.text: Ballas loved Margulis. With his whole person, completely - entirely devoted to her. He would have sacrificed anything and everything for her. His soul, his body, the Orokin Empire. Anything you could possibly dream of.

g.title: j1817452139
g.text: No cost was too great. No morals worth sacrificing. If you had handed him a newborn babe and told him Margulis wished its brains dashed out upon the rocks, it would be dead before you finished your sentence.

g.title: j1611162657
g.text: He would have burned the Origin System to ashes and rebuilt it in her image, Usurper... but herein lies the tragedy.

g.title: j978853342
g.text: Margulis? Aah, Margulis. Dear, sweet, darling Margulis... she still had a conscience.

g.title: j3959368812
g.text: And when she saw the poor Tenno, the poor, Void-torn children...

g.title: j2402048912
g.text: Something in her life was more important than Ballas. Something in her life was worth sacrificing her life for... that was not him.

g.title: j2882343544
g.text: That was not her love for him.

g.title: j2257581740
g.text: And he knew this, my sweet Drifter. He knew this from the moment she laid her eyes on them. And it was driven home when her "mad animals" ensured they were the last she ever saw. Or at least that was what the rumors were amongst us Orokin.

g.title: j2444786070
g.text: Can you imagine the joy amongst the Orokin? Seeing Ballas' precious Archimedean's Void-torn, rabid brats burn out her eyes?

g.title: j411727504
g.text: But I think, it was before then, at the precise moment Margulis fought to save the Tenno that Ballas's heart shattered into a thousand pieces, and never recovered.

g.title: j2814826846
g.text: For he knew he had been supplanted in her own.

g.title: j2368339409
g.text: I suppose for that reason, I pitied him. But the rest of what followed? A love story for the ages... and how it ended in such a broken tragedy.

g.title: j254517622
g.text: I wish you could have seen how they would smile at each other...

g.title: j968596908
g.text: You can romanticize what they had, but that doesn't excuse who he was. Ballas cannot be forgiven for everything he did.

g.title: j3372108214
g.text: I'm glad that their love was real. That he was... complicated back then. And that Margulis wasn't just being played with the whole time.

g.title: j1699902202
g.text: Add 1 to Thermostat counter

g.title: j3391298492
g.text: Add -1 to Thermostat counter

g.title: j4210628397
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j4170352741
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j3575776954
g.text: Nor was I attempting to equate the two, Usurper. I was simply stating that a man could be loved but also capable of terrible things. Ah, well... No hope for the rest of us depraved fools, I suppose...

g.title: j1555611489
g.text: Indeed. Sometimes it brings me peace to think that if even that lord of depravity can find a companion, there is hope for the rest of us, hm? Ha!

g.title: j859312689
g.text: Boolean RoatheMargulis1 is now true.

g.title: j944204197
g.text: But, I have taken enough of your time for the day. Off with you, now.
